newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end lower, extends decline.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end lower, extends decline.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Thursday, extending Wednesday's decline prompted by abundant hydroelectric supplies in the Northwest and weaker natural gas prices.
"There's so much hydro. It pressured COB (California-Oregon Border) and spilled over to PV (Palo Verde)," said a Houston futures trader.
Runoff for January to July on the Columbia River at The Dalles dam in Oregon is forecast to reach 130 percent of average levels, Northwest River Forecast Center said today.

Market sources noted the PV half of the complex and the Southwest cash market were better supported than COB and the Northwest physical market due to a cold snap that covered New Mexico and eastern Arizona this week.
"It's quiet, but it's holding out there," said an East Coast natural gas broker, referring to today's activity in the gas market out West.
February gas deliveries at the San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico finished at $3.17-$3.18 a million British thermal units (mmBtu), slightly higher than Wednesday's $3.15.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas futures settled down $3.2 cents at $3.481/mmBtu, paring an early 26.3 cent loss.
February COB futures finished down 68 cents at $14.03, near its session low of $14.00. March COB ended down 45 cents at $12.85.
February PV futures finished down 32 cents at $3.481 after bouncing between $3.250 and $3.530. March PV ended sharply lower, down 9.0 cents at $3.086.

The Pacific Northwest would enjoy slightly above-normal temperatures through the end of the week, and temperatures in the Southwest would run five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal. Portions of the northern Rockies across Idaho and Montana were expected to see heavy snow in the mountains, Weather Services Corp said in its latest forecast.
Market sources anticipate the complex to continue its fall with little glimmer of a turnaround in the near future.
"It's a slow trend downward," said the Houston trader.
